question.text: Stock exchanges, depositories and clearing corporations are collectively referred to as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.1.3 (i), stock exchanges, depositories and clearing corporations are collectively referred to as Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs). NSE/BSE are MIIs, and their SSE wings operate within this MII construct. The Trap: Option B (Custodians) hold assets on behalf of institutional investors but are not MIIs. Option C (KRAs) maintain KYC records. Option D (AMCs) manage mutual funds. These are all separate intermediary categories. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets Foundation). MIIs are structurally important to understand when tracing SSE listings and settlement. Assessor's Pro-Tip: MIIs carry systemic-importance obligations (SEBI MII Regulations 2018). When engaging with a newly SSE-listed entity, note the specific MII segment (NSE-SSE vs BSE-SSE) — disclosure formats and timelines may differ marginally.
